page.layout: Two printed pages on one scan. Left page: one column of running text, with the printed page number 88 at the head and a running head above the text. Right page: only a narrow strip at the right edge is visible, with cropped text in its margin and outer column. Nothing is printed below the text except the catchword "causa" at the right.

main_text.p: Exillo, inquit, tempore, quo imperatores coeperunt Christiani esse, ecclesiæ negocia ex illorum nutu pendere visa sunt, atque adeo maxima concilia de eorum sententia convocabantur: Item. Octo prima concilia generalia ab imperatoribus erat collecta, & pontifex Romanus ad instar aliorum patriarcharum sacras jusfiones pro veniendo aut mittendo ad concilia recepit.

His adde Franciscum de Victoria tract. de pontifice. Relect. 4. prop. 24. Audi, inquit, quid Johannes de Turrecremata cardinalis tenet, assertor vehementissimus pōtificiæ dignitatis, lib. 3. cap. 10. ubi loquens de utilitate conciliorum; celebratio, inquit, conciliorum utilis est, ad refræнandum exorbitantias quorundam pontificum, qui pontificatum suum aut extra patrum regulas pro voluntate sua exercent, aut simoniacâ pravitate dehonestât, aut vitâ scandalosâ cōfundunt: hac de causa

[Right page, cropped strip, margin fragments only, not legible enough to transcribe reliably: "caufa", "legi", "concilium", "ratorem", "Turrecre", "papæ hoc", "cardinalis", "consilio", "in defensione", "debere inte", "dilis", "Definitionem", "concilio", "vocant" — [illegible, ~120 letters]]

page.notes: Left page: the running head "cordia catholica cap. 25." is set in italic above the text and is treated as the running head; the text beginning "Exillo, inquit," continues from the previous page. The catchword "causa" at the lower right is separate from the text. The text ends on "hac de", where the sentence continues on the next page. A small printer's mark or symbol appears under the text at lower left and is not transcribed. The right page is cut off at the scan edge; only fragments of its outer margin are visible and they are given as illegible above. Spellings such as "jusfiones", "refræнandum" and "dehonestât" are as printed; "refræнandum" has one character I could not confirm and may be a misreading of "refrænandum".
